title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Faces a 9% Jump at the Worst Possible Time for Miners
summary: Key takeaways Bitcoin mining difficulty is on course to rise about 9% on November 27, from 134.82 trillion toward 147 trillion, reversing much of the 9.13% cut on November 14. Under otherwise unchanged conditions, a 9% increase cuts expected BTC output per unit of hashrate by roughly 8.3%. At about $28 per petahash per day, a fleet running at 20 J/TH and $0.05/kWh would see its electricity-adjusted margin fall from about $4 to under $2. The effect is uneven: efficient operators with cheap power can absorb it, while older fleets may switch machines off. Difficulty alone is not evidence of more miner selling; miner balances, exchange transfers and treasury disclosures are. Bitcoin mining difficulty is on course to increase by approximately 9% at the next network adjustment, expected on November 27. The increase would reverse much of the relief miners received less than two weeks ago, leaving operators facing tougher competition for block rewards while Bitcoin trades well below its previous highs. Current network estimates put mining difficulty at 134.82 trillion, following a 9.13% reduction on November 14. If the projected increase holds, difficulty will climb back toward 147 trillion. For miners struggling to keep their machines profitable, the timing is hardly ideal. The electricity bill remains largely unchanged, but the same hardware could soon generate less Bitcoin. Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Is Reversing November’s Relief Bitcoin adjusts its mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to maintain an average block production time of approximately ten minutes. When blocks are produced too quickly, the network makes the mathematical conditions for discovering new blocks more demanding. When production slows, difficulty moves in the opposite direction. The previous 9.13% reduction in Bitcoin mining difficulty gave active miners some breathing room. Operators could expect to earn more Bitcoin from the same amount of computing power, provided other conditions remained comparable. That advantage now appears temporary. The upcoming adjustment, expected at block 977,760, reflects a faster pace of block production during the current difficulty period. A 9% increase in difficulty does not translate into an identical percentage reduction in mining revenue. Under otherwise unchanged conditions, expected Bitcoin production per unit of computing power would decline by approximately 8.3%. Consider an operator whose machines currently generate 1 BTC over a given period. Following a 9% difficulty increase, the same machines would be expected to produce approximately 0.917 BTC over an equivalent period. Nothing about the hardware needs to change for that reduction to occur. The network has simply raised the amount of work required to compete for its rewards. The Real Problem Is What Miners Earn From Their Machines Mining difficulty only tells part of the story. A more useful measure of the industry’s financial condition is hashprice, which tracks the expected revenue generated by a given amount of computing power over a day. Hashprice incorporates Bitcoin’s market value, network difficulty and transaction fee revenue. It provides a clearer indication of whether a miner’s hardware is generating enough income to justify keeping it switched on. Recent network data from mining industry trackers puts daily hashprice at around $28 per petahash of computing power. At that level, the economics can become uncomfortable surprisingly quickly. Consider a hypothetical mining fleet with an energy efficiency of 20 joules per terahash and an electricity rate of $0.05 per kilowatt-hour. Operating one petahash of computing power continuously would cost approximately $24 per day in electricity alone. Against $28 in gross daily mining revenue, that leaves just $4 before hosting, maintenance, cooling, financing and other expenses. If difficulty rises by 9% while Bitcoin’s price and average fees per block remain unchanged, that daily revenue would fall to approximately $25.69. The remaining electricity-adjusted margin would shrink to less than $2. The network adjustment is the same for everyone. Its financial consequences are not. An operator with newer machines and inexpensive power may comfortably absorb the change. Another running older equipment could find that switching off part of its fleet makes more financial sense than continuing to mine. Bitcoin Miners Are Already Rethinking Their Business Models The industry’s response to difficult mining economics extends beyond upgrading machines or negotiating cheaper electricity. Some established Bitcoin mining businesses are redirecting infrastructure toward artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. Access to substantial electricity capacity, established data centers and existing infrastructure gives certain operators alternatives that smaller mining businesses may not have. This does not mean Bitcoin mining is disappearing. The projected difficulty increase itself suggests that blocks are being produced faster than the protocol’s target rate during the current adjustment period. But the growing divergence between mining operators deserves attention. A Bitcoin mining facility with access to inexpensive energy and efficient equipment operates under a very different set of economic conditions from a business relying on expensive financing and aging machines. Rising difficulty does not necessarily make the entire industry unprofitable. It makes the difference between efficient and inefficient operators harder to ignore. Does Higher Mining Difficulty Mean More Bitcoin Selling? The prospect of shrinking margins raises an obvious question for Bitcoin investors: will miners need to sell more BTC to finance their operations? There is a plausible case for additional selling from businesses facing substantial operating expenses or debt repayments. Mining companies cannot generally settle their electricity bills with anticipated future Bitcoin rewards. However, network difficulty alone provides no evidence that miners have increased their Bitcoin sales. Some operators hold substantial treasury reserves. Others sell their production regularly, regardless of market conditions. Businesses can also reduce operating expenses, shut down inefficient equipment or obtain financing instead of liquidating additional holdings. Actual miner balance data, exchange transfers and company treasury disclosures will provide more useful evidence than the difficulty adjustment itself. The immediate development to watch is whether the estimated increase materializes at the next adjustment block. After that, hashprice and changes in network computing power will help reveal how operators are responding. Bitcoin’s protocol is doing exactly what it was designed to do. It adjusts the competition for block rewards without considering whether individual mining businesses can afford to remain competitive. The machines that become uneconomical have always been the operators’ problem, not the network’s.

title: Bitcoin’s Recovery Faces a New Warning After $2 Billion in ETF Outflows
summary: Key takeaways US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $2.05 billion in combined net outflows over four straight sessions ending November 24, per Farside Investors, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for roughly $1.77 billion. Bitcoin is back above $60,000 after trading as low as about $55,300 on November 21, according to Glassnode. Reclaiming $60,000 does not by itself confirm the correction is over: holders who bought near that level may sell into the rebound. Bitcoin trades far beyond US ETFs, so outflows are not proof of further downside, but a recovery that holds despite redemptions would be a stronger signal. Thanksgiving closes US markets, so the missing ETF data is not a sign of improved demand. Friday’s session will be more telling. The Bitcoin recovery above $60,000 is offering some relief after a brutal November sell-off, but the money flowing through US spot Bitcoin ETFs tells a less encouraging story. The funds recorded more than $2 billion in combined net outflows over four consecutive trading sessions ending November 24. Bitcoin’s return to the psychologically important price level follows a difficult week in which the cryptocurrency traded as low as approximately $55,300. The rebound is welcome. What is less clear is whether buyers have returned with enough capital to sustain it. Bitcoin ETFs Are Still Losing Money The scale of the recent withdrawals deserves more attention than the recovery itself. According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $582.3 million on November 19, followed by another $669.2 million the next day. Withdrawals continued on Monday and Tuesday, bringing the combined total across those four trading sessions to approximately $2.05 billion. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for roughly $1.77 billion in net outflows during that period. Wednesday’s figures are still subject to final reporting confirmation, although available data points to further withdrawals. These numbers do not mean that every institutional investor is abandoning Bitcoin. ETF shareholders include different types of investors, from financial advisers and asset managers to individual traders. Some may be reducing risk, while others could be unwinding positions that were never intended as long-term investments. What the figures establish is that the ETF market has experienced persistent net redemptions, even after Bitcoin’s substantial decline. That is not the response bulls would ideally want to see from buyers following a major correction. Bitcoin’s Drop Below $60,000 Exposed a Deeper Problem Earlier this week, Bitcoin fell below $60,000 again after an initial recovery above $64,000 failed to hold. Glassnode’s November 24 report, titled The Canary in the Coal Mine, documented the severity of Bitcoin’s latest decline. The cryptocurrency reached approximately $55,300 on November 21, falling beneath the lows established during the summer. That matters because investors who bought during previous corrections may now be sitting on losses despite having entered the market at what appeared to be relatively attractive prices. Glassnode’s historical data reveals another uncomfortable detail. Long-term holders recently accounted for more than 75% of Bitcoin’s realized losses before their share fell back toward 50%. Similar periods of selling at a loss appeared during previous bear markets, although that alone does not establish that Bitcoin has reached a bottom. Their behavior becomes particularly important when Bitcoin starts recovering. Some holders may use a rebound to reduce their exposure or exit positions closer to their original purchase price. Others may be willing to hold through further volatility. Which group dominates will influence how much buying is required to sustain the next move higher. A price that previously attracted buyers can become an area of selling pressure when the market approaches it from below. This is one reason why reclaiming $60,000 should not automatically be interpreted as confirmation that the correction has ended. A Market Bottom Does Not Require Everyone to Turn Bullish There is a credible argument against interpreting persistent ETF outflows as evidence that Bitcoin must fall further. Markets can begin recovering before investor sentiment improves. In fact, waiting for every major indicator to turn positive can mean missing a substantial portion of a reversal. Glassnode’s latest research offers some historical perspective. Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to capital inflows over the preceding year have reached their highest intensity since the FTX collapse in 2022. Previous episodes of heavy losses have occurred near major market bottoms, but severe selling alone is not enough to confirm that a recovery is underway. Bitcoin also trades across a much broader market than US exchange-traded funds. Direct purchases, overseas exchanges and other investment vehicles can absorb selling even when American funds experience redemptions. The distinction is between evidence that a market can recover and evidence that it has already established a sustainable recovery. Bitcoin’s latest bounce demonstrates that buyers are willing to step in at lower prices. It does not yet establish whether those buyers can absorb additional selling at higher levels. If Bitcoin begins to hold its gains despite persistent ETF withdrawals, that would itself be an encouraging development. It would suggest that demand elsewhere in the market is capable of offsetting some of the pressure coming from the funds. For now, the price and ETF data leave that question open. Thanksgiving Could Make Bitcoin’s Next Move Harder to Read Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday adds another complication to the recovery. US equity markets are closed, removing a regular trading session for American spot Bitcoin ETFs while cryptocurrency exchanges continue operating. The absence of new ETF flow figures during the holiday should not be confused with an improvement in institutional demand. With fewer traditional financial market participants active, Bitcoin’s immediate price movements may also provide an incomplete picture of how investors are responding to the recent sell-off. Friday’s shortened US trading session and the subsequent return to normal market hours will provide more useful evidence. For traders, the important signals are whether Bitcoin can retain its recent gains, whether ETF redemptions begin to ease and whether buying remains strong enough to absorb selling when normal market participation resumes. The $60,000 level may dominate the headlines, but the more convincing recovery will be the one that can survive without depending entirely on temporary relief from selling pressure.

title: Fidelity Files for Chainlink ETF. What Does It Mean for LINK?
summary: Key takeaways Fidelity has filed to launch a Chainlink ETF (ticker FLNK) that would hold LINK directly and list on Nasdaq, but the filing is preliminary with no launch date or final fee. The fund would not stake its LINK, so shareholders would not receive staking rewards. Fidelity would enter a market that already has Grayscale (GLNK) and Bitwise (CLNK) LINK funds, and Charles Schwab offers direct LINK trading. A new listing does not automatically mean new LINK buying: only sustained net creations add to the fund’s holdings. Shares outstanding, LINK held and net creations after launch will show whether demand is genuinely new. Fidelity’s Chainlink ETF proposal would hold LINK directly and trade on Nasdaq if it clears the remaining steps. The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, described in a November 25 registration statement, would use the ticker FLNK, although the filing is preliminary and no launch date or final annual fee has been provided. The larger question is not whether Wall Street can package LINK. It already has. The question is whether Fidelity can attract fresh demand for the token rather than divide the existing market among another set of fund shares. Fidelity’s Filing Is Specific About What Investors Would Own The proposed fund would hold LINK, not a basket of blockchain companies or derivatives intended to mimic LINK’s price. Its objective is to follow the token’s U.S. dollar performance, less expenses and liabilities. The prospectus identifies Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody as custodians, with the trust intending to hold its LINK on Ethereum. Fidelity also lays out how the price would be measured. Its proposed reference rate uses prices from eligible LINK spot markets, with a volume-weighted median methodology calculated every 15 seconds using rolling 60-minute market data. That is a mechanism for valuing the assets. It is not a guarantee that fund shares will trade at precisely the reported value when markets are thin or volatile. Nor is this a yield product. The filing states plainly: “The Trust will not stake its LINK.” Shareholders would not receive staking rewards through the fund. They would be buying securities designed to reflect an underlying token’s price, not a wallet balance they can use in Chainlink services. That distinction matters because the company’s use of Chainlink technology elsewhere is a separate story. NewsBTC has previously reported on Chainlink infrastructure used with Fidelity’s tokenized FILQ fund. An investment vehicle that owns LINK is not evidence of increased demand for Chainlink’s oracle services, and using the network’s technology does not automatically mean buying its token. Fidelity Would Enter a Market That Already Has LINK Funds This is not the first attempt to make LINK available through conventional securities accounts. Grayscale’s Chainlink Trust ETF, trading as GLNK, had a share creation and redemption program in place from December 2025, according to its SEC disclosures. The Bitwise Chainlink ETF, CLNK, also appeared in a January 2026 Nasdaq information circular. And fund shares are not the only conventional route. In November, NewsBTC covered Charles Schwab’s rollout of direct LINK trading to eligible crypto clients. These routes do different things, but they establish a useful baseline: access is no longer the same problem it was when crypto products were confined to specialist exchanges. Fidelity’s possible advantage is distribution. Its name and brokerage relationships may reach customers who would not open a crypto wallet or buy LINK on a trading platform. That is a credible reason the filing matters. But branding, however recognizable, cannot tell investors how much money will arrive once trading begins. There is also the price of access. The preliminary prospectus leaves the sponsor’s annual fee blank. Until that figure is settled, it is impossible to make an honest cost comparison with competing LINK products. For investors choosing between wrappers around the same token, fees, trading spreads and the gap between share prices and net asset value deserve more attention than a new ticker. A New ETF Listing Would Not Automatically Mean New LINK Buying The mechanics are worth getting right. The proposed trust would issue and redeem large blocks of shares through authorized participants, using cash or LINK under procedures described in the filing. Everyday investors would generally trade the shares on an exchange instead of placing orders with the trust. Those are two different markets. When one investor sells an existing fund share to another, the trade does not by itself require the trust to acquire more LINK. Sustained net creations can increase a fund’s underlying holdings. Redemptions can do the reverse. A rising share price, meanwhile, may reflect a higher LINK price rather than additional tokens entering custody. That is why the announcement alone provides no evidence of fresh institutional inflows. The Form S-1 is a plan, not a subscription report. It does not tell us how much outside capital will be committed, what portion might come from rival products, or whether investor interest will survive a difficult crypto market. There is a fair counterargument. Fidelity could appeal to a materially different pool of investors and grow total demand rather than simply redistribute it. The filing establishes a possible channel for that to happen. It does not establish the outcome. What Would Actually Change the Assessment? First, the registration statement must become effective and the proposed Nasdaq listing must move forward. The final prospectus should also resolve the missing fee and other commercial details. Those are immediate milestones, not formalities to be assumed away. If the product launches, the more revealing evidence will arrive afterward: the number of LINK held, changes in shares outstanding, sustained net creations or redemptions, trading liquidity and discounts or premiums to net asset value. Comparisons with existing LINK funds would help separate fresh demand from investors moving between products. Until those figures exist, the sensible interpretation is narrow. Fidelity wants to sell investors exposure to Chainlink through a familiar brokerage format. Whether that changes the market for LINK is still an open question, and one that a filing cannot answer.

title: HyroTrader Adds Hyro Core From $9 and No-Evaluation Hyro Instant to Rebuilt Crypto Prop Platform
summary: The new accounts follow an October overhaul that brought the firm’s own trading terminal, AI-agent trading, BloFin and static loss limits on every challenge DUBAI, UAE, November 2026: HyroTrader, a crypto proprietary trading firm, has launched two new ways to get a funded trading account. Hyro Core is a one-phase challenge from $9, and Hyro Instant skips the challenge altogether. Both went on sale on 4 November 2026. They are the second step of a rebuild that began in October. That month HyroTrader launched its own trading terminal with stock and index contracts and opened accounts on it to AI trading agents. It also added BloFin as a second exchange, made every loss limit static and made its payouts easier to verify on a public dashboard. Firms like HyroTrader give traders a funded account and pay them a share of the profit made on it. Traders usually earn that account by passing a paid trading test, known as a challenge. At HyroTrader, every account, funded or not, is a simulated (demo) account running on live market data. The payouts are real money, paid as a share of the simulated profit. Hyro Instant is the bigger change for a firm that until now funded only traders who passed a challenge. “Without an evaluation, a firm cannot establish whether a trader has a consistent track record or simply had a few successful trades,” HyroTrader said in announcing Hyro Instant. “Nevertheless, the demand for a faster route is clear.” Hyro Core is the firm’s lowest-priced challenge. A $2,500 account costs $9, and the largest, $100,000, costs $349. Against One-Step, the firm’s other one-phase challenge, it pairs the lower price with tighter loss limits. To pass, a trader needs a 10% profit over at least four trading days, with no single day counting for more than 40% of it. The challenge ends if the account loses more than 3% of its starting balance in a day, or 5% in total. Both limits are static, which means they stay fixed to the starting balance and do not rise as the account gains. Funded Hyro Core traders receive a fixed 80% of the profit as payouts. The fee is not refunded once the challenge is activated. “A trader’s budget does not necessarily reflect their motivation or skill,” HyroTrader said in announcing Hyro Core. Hyro Instant, a funded account with no evaluation. Image: HyroTrader Hyro Instant has no test at all. After identity verification and account setup, the trader receives a funded account with no profit target to reach. It costs from $169 for a $5,000 account to $2,799 for $100,000. It keeps Hyro Core’s daily and total loss limits and adds a per-trade limit. No single trade may lose more than 2% of the starting balance. A first breach of that trade limit brings a warning, and a second closes the account. The first payout opens after three qualifying trading days (days on which the trader closes at least one trade above set size and price-move thresholds), with the account in profit. The profit split starts at 80% and can rise to 90% at the firm’s discretion. The fee is refunded only if identity verification is not approved. Both new accounts run on what HyroTrader built in October. At the centre is the Hyro platform, the firm’s own trading terminal, which needs no exchange account. It offers more than 700 perpetual futures markets (contracts with no expiry date) on live prices. Besides crypto, they include contracts on stocks such as Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, on the S&P 500, and on gold and silver. Traders who prefer an exchange can instead run any programme on their own demo account at Bybit or, since October, at BloFin. HyroTrader says that in 2023 it became the first crypto prop firm to let traders run a challenge on their own exchange demo account. On the Hyro platform, Hyro Instant accounts included, traders can also connect their own AI agent through MCP, the Model Context Protocol (an open standard for linking AI tools to other software). The agent places trades for the trader’s own strategy under the account’s usual rules, and the trader can revoke its access at any time. The October rebuild also made payouts easier to check. HyroTrader lists the payouts it sends on the Solana blockchain on a public transparency page, each with a link to its blockchain record unless the trader has chosen to hide it. In November the minimum payout fell from $100 to $25. The firm also eased its existing challenges in the same week. One-Step challenges bought from 5 November need at least three trading days instead of five and allow an 8% total loss limit instead of 6%. Two-Step challenges bought from 4 November need four trading days in each phase instead of five. About HyroTrader HyroTrader is a crypto prop firm launched in 2023 and operating from Dubai, UAE. Traders take a challenge or start funded with Hyro Instant, receive 80% of their profits as payouts, up to 90% on some programmes, and are usually paid in stablecoins within 24 hours. According to HyroTrader’s public payout transparency page, the firm has paid more than $9.5 million in profit splits to traders since 2023, as of November 2026. More than $1.6 million of that went out on the Solana blockchain. HyroTrader says it has funded more than 1,700 traders. HyroTrader is not a broker and does not provide investment services or advice. All trading takes place on simulated accounts. Media contact HyroTrader support@hyrotrader.com www.hyrotrader.com

title: Prop Firm Payouts Near $2 Billion: 10 Best Prop Firms In 2026
summary: Key takeaways Tracked prop firm payouts are nearing $1.97 billion across 45 firms since October 2023, with more than $115 million recorded in November alone, according to Payout Junction. Payout totals show that payments occurred, not that the average trader is profitable after challenge fees, resets and subscriptions. A $100,000 futures account with a $3,000 maximum drawdown leaves very little room for error; compare loss allowances and profit targets, not account size. Consistency rules, payout buffers, withdrawal caps and trailing drawdowns can stop a profitable trader from withdrawing. The guide compares ten firms across forex, futures and crypto based on published rules, not firsthand testing. Payouts are never guaranteed. Prop firm payouts are approaching the $2 billion mark, with data from Payout Junction showing nearly $1.97 billion in cumulative payments across 45 tracked firms since October 2023. More than $115 million has been recorded in November 2026 alone. The figures offer a glimpse into how large the funded trading industry has become. But finding the best prop firms in 2026 requires looking at something payout leaderboards rarely tell you: what traders actually have to go through to get paid. A $100,000 futures account with a $3,000 maximum drawdown gives a trader just $3,000 of room for error. Add consistency requirements, withdrawal caps and restrictions on trading strategies, and two accounts with identical advertised balances can offer very different trading conditions. The industry is also expanding beyond its traditional forex and futures markets. New platforms are introducing prop trading for cryptocurrencies and tokenized stocks, giving traders access to a wider range of markets without having to commit the full advertised account balance themselves. For this guide, we examine ten prop firms across forex, futures and cryptocurrency markets, looking beyond advertised profit splits to compare evaluation rules, trading conditions, costs and payout eligibility. Editorial disclosure: This guide is based on published trading rules, product documentation and available payout data. Traders can lose their challenge fees, and most retail funded trading programs initially use simulated accounts. Receiving a payout is not guaranteed. Best Prop Firms In 2026 At A Glance Prop firm Markets Best suited to Main consideration FTMO Forex and CFDs Traditional evaluation models Higher first-phase target FundedNext CFDs and futures Variety of account models Different reward conditions FundingPips Forex and CFDs Flexible payout preferences Strategy and consistency restrictions The5ers Forex Longer-term account development Program-specific growth rules Hola Prime CFDs and futures Platform choice Withdrawal fees and eligibility Topstep Futures Structured futures trading Payout caps and loss limits Tradeify Futures Choice of payout structure Permanent funded-plan selection Take Profit Trader Futures Frequent withdrawals Funded account buffer Lucid Trading Futures Flexible funded-stage rules Payout objectives and caps HyroTrader Crypto Crypto-native trading Volatility and drawdown restrictions The firms are grouped by their suitability for different trading styles rather than ranked by a single payout leaderboard. Prop Firm Payouts Approach $2 Billion According to Payout Junction’s November 24 data, approximately 1.19 million payout transactions have been matched to public blockchain records since October 2023. The tracker covers 45 firms, although its figures do not necessarily represent all payments made by those businesses. Bank transfers and other payments outside its blockchain tracking coverage may not appear in the dataset. November has already recorded roughly $115.5 million in tracked payments across more than 91,000 transactions. These are substantial figures, but they need context. A firm paying out $50 million does not necessarily offer a better opportunity than one paying out $5 million. The larger business could simply have more customers, higher fees or a larger number of accounts. Chart by NewsBTC, data from Payout Junction, November 16–22, 2026. Tracked blockchain payments only. Nor do the figures tell us how much traders collectively spent on challenges, resets and subscriptions before receiving those payouts. Without that information, it is impossible to determine the industry’s aggregate profitability for traders. Payout data is useful evidence that payments have occurred. It is not evidence that the average customer makes money. That distinction matters when comparing the following firms. 1. FTMO — Best For Traditional Evaluation Traders FTMO offers a conventional two-phase evaluation for traders who prefer clearly defined profit objectives and fixed overall loss limits. Its two-step model requires a 10% profit target during the first phase and 5% during verification. The maximum daily loss is 5% of the initial simulated capital, while the overall loss limit is 10%. For a $100,000 evaluation, that translates into a $10,000 first-phase profit target and a $10,000 maximum overall loss allowance. FTMO Trading Conditions Evaluation: Two phases under its traditional model. Profit targets: 10% and 5%. Maximum daily loss: 5%. Maximum overall loss: 10%. Funded environment: Simulated trading under contractual reward conditions. FTMO also offers a separate one-step model. Traders should not assume that its rules are identical to the traditional challenge. The two-step structure may appeal to traders whose strategies require more breathing room than accounts with narrow trailing loss limits. The first-phase target, however, requires meaningful performance relative to the allowed drawdown. Pros Conventional evaluation structure. Clearly documented trading objectives. Static overall loss allowance on the two-step model. No minimum trading-days requirement on the subsequent two-step FTMO Account. Cons A 10% initial profit target can be demanding. Restrictions differ between account types. Challenge fees remain at risk if the trader breaches the rules. Our view FTMO is worth considering for traders with an existing, tested forex or CFD strategy. Its two-step structure is easier to assess mathematically than many trailing-drawdown alternatives, although that does not make it easy to pass. 2. FundedNext — Best For Account Model Variety FundedNext operates across CFDs and futures, offering several routes to funded-style trading. Its Stellar 2-Step model is particularly interesting for traders who want a traditional evaluation with relatively conventional risk limits. The first phase requires an 8% return, followed by 5% in verification. Both phases apply a 5% daily loss limit and 10% maximum overall loss. The published rules specify five minimum trading days per phase. FundedNext Trading Conditions Representative model: Stellar 2-Step. Profit targets: 8% and 5%. Maximum daily loss: 5%. Maximum overall loss: 10%. Minimum trading days: Five per evaluation phase. The firm also offers alternative CFD challenge formats and futures evaluations. One area worth examining is its performance reward policy. Reward frequency and eligibility can vary according to the option selected, with some routes requiring a specific number of profitable trading days. This makes comparing the headline profit split alone insufficient. Pros Multiple routes across different markets. Traditional two-step model with an 8% initial target. Different reward arrangements. Detailed online help documentation. Cons Rules vary considerably between products. Some reward options impose additional profitable-day requirements. Promotional benefits and account add-ons may change the total cost. Our view FundedNext’s strongest feature is choice. Its biggest complication is also choice. Traders should compare the funded-stage conditions of each product before deciding which evaluation to purchase. 3. FundingPips — Best For Traders Comparing Payout Options FundingPips offers several evaluation models, including one-step, two-step and evaluation-free alternatives. Its 2-Step Standard model requires an 8% profit target followed by 5% in verification. The firm’s current documentation also confirms that the previous optional 10% first-phase target was discontinued on July 24, 2026. FundingPips Trading Conditions Representative model: 2-Step Standard. Profit targets: 8% and 5%. Maximum daily loss: 5%. Maximum overall loss: 10%. Additional conditions: Dependent on the selected reward cycle. FundingPips is an example of why traders must pay attention to changes in prop firm rules. Its Standard model documentation applies a 35% consistency condition to the on-demand reward cycle. This means a trader who generates most of their profit during one unusually successful session could need additional trading before qualifying for a withdrawal. That might suit a strategy producing relatively steady returns. It could be less suitable for traders whose profits are concentrated around a handful of strong market opportunities. Pros Multiple evaluation routes. Different reward-cycle choices. Competitive first-phase target on the Standard model. Extensive model-specific documentation. Cons Certain withdrawal options have consistency conditions. Strategy restrictions require careful review. Older account descriptions may no longer reflect current rules. Our view FundingPips deserves consideration for its payout flexibility, but traders should examine the conditions attached to their preferred withdrawal cycle rather than choosing whichever option advertises the highest reward share. 4. The5ers — Best For Longer-Term Account Development The5ers offers several forex-focused evaluation and account-development programs. Its High Stakes program is built around a two-stage evaluation and subsequent growth opportunities. The firm distinguishes between different versions of High Stakes, making it important to identify the exact account being purchased rather than relying on older comparisons. The5ers Trading Conditions Representative model: High Stakes. Evaluation: Two phases. Drawdown: Program and account-specific limits. Account growth: Subject to published scaling conditions. Withdrawal eligibility: Dependent on the funded program. The appeal of The5ers is its focus on account development over time. Traders who already have a strategy capable of producing steady returns may find growth-oriented programs more interesting than accounts designed primarily around rapid evaluations. However, scaling opportunities should not be treated as guaranteed increases in accessible trading capital. The trader must meet the conditions attached to the program, and trading restrictions continue to apply. Pros Programs designed around longer-term account development. Published rules for growth and profitable trading days. Forex-focused product selection. Different evaluation structures. Cons Growth conditions can extend the time required to increase account size. Different program versions complicate comparisons. News-trading restrictions require attention. Our view The5ers is a reasonable candidate for patient forex traders who value gradual account development. Its suitability depends on the precise High Stakes version and the trader’s ability to satisfy its growth criteria. 5. Hola Prime — Best For Traders Seeking Platform Choice Hola Prime offers multiple evaluation formats across forex, CFDs and futures. Its 2-Step Prime challenge requires an 8% profit target during the first phase and 5% during the second, with at least three trading days in each phase. The firm’s published schedules also differentiate risk limits according to account size. Hola Prime Trading Conditions Representative model: 2-Step Prime. Profit targets: 8% and 5%. Minimum trading days: Three per phase. Maximum overall loss: Generally 10%, with 8% applying to the $200,000 tier. Daily loss: Account-specific. Hola Prime’s product range gives traders alternatives to the standard evaluation experience. However, account fees, platform access and withdrawal terms differ across models. Its advertised challenge-fee refund also comes with conditions. Under the reviewed 2-Step Prime terms, the refund is distributed across the first four successful payouts rather than returned immediately upon passing. That is an important detail for anyone calculating how much they need to earn before recovering their initial expenses. Pros Multiple forex and futures programs. Broad platform selection across products. Relatively short minimum evaluation period. Published reference tables for account rules. Cons Larger accounts can carry tighter percentage-based loss limits. Challenge-fee refunds require successful payouts. Withdrawal charges and reward conditions vary. Our view Hola Prime is worth comparing if trading platform choice matters to you. Just remember that a fast payout-processing promise begins after a withdrawal becomes eligible, not necessarily after your first profitable trade. 6. Topstep — Best For Structured Futures Trading Topstep is focused on futures trading through its Trading Combine and subsequent funded-account structure. Unlike a traditional CFD evaluation, the maximum loss allowance is relatively small compared with the advertised account size. Its published Trading Combine parameters include maximum loss limits of $2,000 for a $50,000 account, $3,000 for a $100,000 account and $4,500 for a $150,000 account. Topstep Trading Conditions Account size Maximum loss allowance $50,000 $2,000 $100,000 $3,000 $150,000 $4,500 A trader purchasing the $50,000 option is not receiving $50,000 that can be lost while testing a strategy. The relevant initial risk allowance is $2,000. After passing the Trading Combine, traders can progress to an Express Funded Account, which is a simulated funded-stage account. Its payout policy includes conditions relating to withdrawal eligibility, payout limits and changes to the maximum loss threshold after withdrawals. Pros Dedicated futures trading environment. Explicit dollar-based maximum loss limits. Structured progression beyond the evaluation. Extensive educational and support documentation. Cons Narrow loss allowances relative to advertised account balances. Withdrawals can alter the account’s remaining risk cushion. Evaluation and funded-stage conditions differ. Our view Topstep is worth considering for futures traders who prefer a structured environment. Anyone moving from forex prop trading should first understand how dollar-based trailing loss limits differ from percentage-based static drawdowns. 7. Tradeify — Best For Choosing A Funded Payout Structure Tradeify offers futures evaluations with different routes into funded-stage trading. Its Select evaluation does not impose a daily loss limit during the evaluation but does apply a consistency requirement. After passing, traders choose between Select Flex and Select Daily payout policies. Tradeify Trading Conditions Representative model: Select. Market: Futures. Evaluation daily loss limit: None under the reviewed Select rules. Evaluation consistency: Applicable. Funded payout options: Select Flex or Select Daily. The ability to select a payout arrangement is attractive because not every trader earns profits in the same way. A trader producing relatively consistent daily returns may prefer a different structure from someone whose strategy depends on occasional larger moves. However, the choice is permanent for that funded account, according to Tradeify’s official payout policy. Changing to the alternative arrangement requires obtaining another qualifying account. Pros Choice of funded-stage payout arrangements. No daily loss limit during the reviewed Select evaluation. Dedicated futures trading. Published explanations of account-specific withdrawal conditions. Cons Evaluation consistency requirements still apply. Funded payout-policy selection is permanent. Drawdown and withdrawal conditions must be compared separately. Our view Tradeify’s Select model is particularly interesting because it allows traders to choose how they want to approach withdrawals after evaluation. That flexibility is only valuable if the trader understands both options before selecting one. 8. Take Profit Trader — Best For Frequent Withdrawal Opportunities Take Profit Trader offers futures trading programs built around an evaluation, a simulated PRO account and potential progression to a live-market PRO+ account. The firm published updated plan information on November 23, 2026, making older descriptions of its account rules particularly important to recheck. Its current product announcement describes three-day evaluations, frequent PRO withdrawals and no funded-stage consistency rule under the new plans. Take Profit Trader Trading Conditions Market: Futures. Evaluation: Single phase. Minimum evaluation period: Three trading days under the new plans. Evaluation consistency requirement: 50%. PRO withdrawal availability: Daily, subject to buffer requirements. Funded-stage consistency: None under the new plans. The buffer is the detail traders should examine most closely. The firm allows eligible traders to withdraw profits above the required buffer. Consequently, a trader can have a profitable account without necessarily being able to withdraw all that profit while retaining the account. Legacy accounts may also remain subject to their original terms. Pros Frequent withdrawal opportunities. No funded-stage consistency condition under the reviewed new plans. Single-phase futures evaluation. A route to live-market trading through PRO+. Cons PRO buffer requirements must be satisfied. Legacy and newer accounts can operate under different rules. Futures-only product offering. Our view Take Profit Trader stands out for its withdrawal model. Traders interested in frequent payouts should still calculate how much profit must remain in the account before treating those earnings as spendable income. 9. Lucid Trading — Best For Flexible Funded-Stage Rules Lucid Trading offers several futures account models, including LucidPro, LucidFlex, LucidDirect and LucidDaily. Its LucidFlex program is particularly relevant to traders who want to avoid funded-stage profit-concentration restrictions. According to the firm’s LucidFlex documentation, the funded account does not impose a consistency rule or a separate payout buffer. The published profit-sharing arrangement is 90% for the trader. Lucid Trading Conditions Representative model: LucidFlex. Market: Futures. Funded-stage consistency: None. Reward share: 90%. Separate payout buffer: None. Withdrawal eligibility: Subject to qualifying objectives and account rules. The absence of a consistency rule does not mean traders can withdraw unrestricted amounts whenever they choose. LucidFlex still has specific payout conditions, including requirements that must be satisfied before a withdrawal is approved. Traders must also consider how a payout affects the account’s maximum loss threshold. Pros No funded-stage consistency rule on LucidFlex. No separate payout buffer on that model. 90% advertised reward share. Multiple futures account structures. Cons Payout objectives continue to apply. Withdrawal caps and qualifying conditions need examination. Other Lucid products have different requirements. Our view LucidFlex may appeal to traders who dislike having their profitable sessions constrained by a consistency formula. That makes the account more flexible in one respect, not necessarily less risky overall. 10. HyroTrader — Best For Crypto-Native Prop Trading HyroTrader focuses on cryptocurrency traders rather than adapting a traditional forex evaluation to include a limited selection of digital assets. Its one-step program requires a 10% profit target, with a 4% daily drawdown and 6% maximum overall loss under the published model. The firm also offers alternative evaluation formats, including its recently introduced lower-cost Hyro Core program. HyroTrader Trading Conditions Representative model: One-Step. Market: Cryptocurrency. Profit target: 10%. Daily drawdown: 4%. Maximum overall loss: 6%. Standard minimum trading days: Five on the reviewed One-Step model. The attraction is that traders can use crypto-oriented trading infrastructure and market data rather than relying exclusively on a conventional forex platform. For traders unfamiliar with derivatives, our guide to long and short positions in crypto explains how leverage and liquidation affect market exposure. HyroTrader’s trading rules also clarify that allocated challenge and funded-account balances are simulated. Payouts represent a contractual share of eligible simulated trading performance. That distinction matters because the term funded account is frequently misunderstood. Pros Cryptocurrency-focused trading experience. Multiple evaluation options. Exchange-demo integration on supported setups. Detailed risk and trading-rule documentation. Cons A 10% target against a 6% overall loss limit is demanding. Cryptocurrency volatility can make tight loss limits difficult to manage. Account-specific strategy and payout restrictions apply. Our view HyroTrader is worth examining for traders who already specialize in crypto markets. It is less compelling for someone whose only reason for choosing crypto is the belief that higher volatility makes a challenge easier to pass. How The Best Prop Firms Compare By Trading Style There is no single account structure that suits everyone. Trading preference Firms worth comparing Traditional forex evaluations FTMO, FundedNext Lower first-phase profit targets FundingPips, FundedNext, Hola Prime Account development and scaling The5ers Flexible futures payout arrangements Tradeify Frequent eligible withdrawals Take Profit Trader No funded-stage consistency rule on selected models LucidFlex, Take Profit Trader Structured futures evaluations Topstep Crypto-focused trading HyroTrader Variety of evaluation products FundedNext, Hola Prime, FundingPips These selections reflect specific published product features, not independently measured payout approval rates or guarantees of superior results. The Number Most Prop Traders Should Pay More Attention To The advertised account balance is usually one of the least informative numbers in a prop firm comparison. Consider two hypothetical accounts: Trading condition Account A Account B Advertised balance $100,000 $50,000 Profit target $6,000 $3,000 Maximum loss allowance $3,000 $5,000 Target divided by loss allowance 2.0 0.6 Account A offers twice the advertised balance of Account B. Yet it provides less room for losses and requires a substantially higher profit relative to that allowance. This does not establish the probability of passing either challenge. That depends on the strategy, trading costs, risk management and other account rules. It does show why choosing the largest advertised account is not always sensible. The calculation becomes more complicated when an account uses trailing drawdown. Static Vs. Trailing Drawdown A static maximum loss threshold remains anchored to a specified balance under the account’s rules. A trailing drawdown moves upward as the trader generates profits, potentially reducing the room available for a subsequent losing streak. Intraday trailing drawdown is particularly important because some models adjust the threshold based on unrealized profits. A trade that briefly gains $1,000 before closing with a much smaller profit can therefore affect the trader’s remaining loss allowance. Two firms advertising the same maximum drawdown can offer very different practical conditions depending on how and when that threshold moves. Why A Profitable Trader Can Still Miss Out On A Payout Passing an evaluation is generally only the first stage. The rules that determine whether someone receives a withdrawal can be more restrictive than the initial profit targets. Consistency Requirements A consistency rule limits how much of the qualifying profit can come from a single trading session or another defined period. For example, suppose a trader earns $2,000 during their best day and finishes the payout cycle with $4,000 in qualifying profit. That best day represents 50% of the total. Under a hypothetical 40% consistency requirement, total qualifying profit would need to reach at least $5,000, assuming the best day remains unchanged and the rule uses this particular calculation. The trader may have to continue trading even though they are already profitable. Payout Buffers And Withdrawal Caps Some firms require profits to remain in an account as a buffer against future losses. Others limit how much traders can withdraw during their initial payout cycles. These restrictions are not necessarily unreasonable. A firm may want traders to demonstrate sustained performance before allowing larger withdrawals. But customers should know exactly what they are buying. There is a considerable difference between advertising daily payouts and allowing a trader to withdraw every dollar earned that day. Prohibited Trading Strategies Account agreements can restrict copy trading, certain automated strategies, cross-account hedging, account sharing, news trading and other trading behaviors. The precise definitions differ between firms. Before paying for an account, traders should review both the public trading objectives and the account agreement governing payout eligibility. A strategy permitted during evaluation may have different conditions after funding. How Much Do Prop Firm Challenges Really Cost? The advertised challenge price is only the initial expense. Depending on the firm and product, customers may also incur subscription charges, reset fees, funded-account activation fees, market-data fees, platform costs or withdrawal-processing charges. Promotional discounts can make the first purchase attractive without necessarily reducing the cost of subsequent attempts. Consider a hypothetical trader who purchases four $100 challenges before successfully qualifying for a funded account. That trader has spent $400 before accounting for any additional charges. The first $300 payout would not mean the trader has made a net profit from prop trading. Their total challenge expenditure would still exceed their withdrawals. This is another reason the industry’s approaching $2 billion payout milestone should not be confused with $2 billion in net trader earnings. How We Selected These Prop Firms Our editorial assessment considers the following factors: Evaluation design: How the profit targets compare with the available loss allowance. Drawdown mechanics: Whether thresholds are static, trailing, intraday or adjusted after withdrawals. Payout eligibility: The conditions that must be met before traders can withdraw. Cost transparency: Challenge fees, recurring charges, resets and other expenses. Trading infrastructure: Supported markets, available platforms and product accessibility. Rule transparency: Whether current trading restrictions and account agreements are readily available. Account suitability: Which trading styles are compatible with each product. The selection is based on documentary research rather than a claim that NewsBTC has personally purchased, traded or withdrawn money from every program. Reported payouts are considered supporting evidence of industry activity, not a standalone measure of reliability. Are Prop Firms Legitimate? Retail prop firms generally offer traders access to an evaluation or simulated trading program in exchange for a fee. Belgium’s financial regulator, the FSMA, has also published a consumer warning about retail prop trading programs, highlighting the risks of paying for repeated challenges. Participants who meet the contractual requirements may receive monetary rewards linked to their trading performance. Some businesses subsequently move qualifying traders into live-market accounts. This is different from opening a conventional brokerage account with personal deposited trading capital. It also means traders should examine who operates the program, which legal entity they contract with, where disputes are handled and what happens if the provider changes its rules or ceases operations. A large number of successful payout transactions does not guarantee that every valid withdrawal will be approved, nor does it establish the financial health of the company. Before buying a challenge, traders should read the current agreement, establish their eligibility and understand which circumstances can lead to account termination. Frequently Asked Questions What Is The Best Prop Firm In 2026? FTMO and FundedNext are worth comparing for traditional forex evaluations. Topstep, Tradeify, Take Profit Trader and Lucid Trading offer different futures trading structures, while HyroTrader is focused on cryptocurrency. The most suitable firm depends on the trader’s strategy, risk tolerance, market preference and withdrawal requirements. Which Prop Firms Have Daily Payouts? Take Profit Trader offers daily eligible withdrawals under its reviewed PRO model, subject to the required buffer. Tradeify also offers a Select Daily payout arrangement. Daily availability does not remove other eligibility conditions. Which Prop Firms Have No Consistency Rule? LucidFlex does not impose a funded-stage consistency rule under its published terms. Take Profit Trader’s new PRO plans also advertise no funded-stage consistency requirement. Evaluation-stage restrictions may still apply. What Is The Best Crypto Prop Firm? HyroTrader is one of the crypto-focused firms worth researching because its programs are built around digital-asset trading. Traders should compare cryptocurrency market access, drawdown calculations, exchange integrations and payout eligibility before selecting a program. Can You Lose Money With A Prop Firm? Yes. Traders can lose evaluation fees, subscriptions, reset fees and other charges without ever receiving a payout. The simulated nature of many funded accounts does not eliminate the financial risk of paying for repeated evaluations. Are Prop Firm Payouts Guaranteed? No. Withdrawals depend on the firm’s contractual requirements, trading-rule compliance and ability to make payments. Historical payout figures do not guarantee future withdrawals. Final Verdict The prop trading industry has grown considerably, and nearly $2 billion in tracked payouts demonstrates that substantial sums are changing hands. What it does not demonstrate is how many traders are profitable after accounting for their expenses. The best prop firm is not necessarily the one paying the most money, offering the largest account or advertising the highest profit split. It is the one whose evaluation and funded-stage rules are compatible with a trader’s existing strategy. Before purchasing a challenge, calculate how much room the account actually provides for losses, how much profit must be generated before a withdrawal becomes possible and how much repeated attempts could cost. Those numbers are considerably more useful than the advertised account balance.

title: Microsoft’s ‘Code Red’ Exposes Crypto’s Own Cloud Problem
summary: Key takeaways Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” to overhaul its engineering and crisis response after a global outage on November 12-13 that lasted about 24 hours. Coinbase’s May outage was traced to a cooling failure in an AWS data center: all five matching engine nodes were in the same building, and three went offline, disrupting trading, deposits and withdrawals for about eight hours. Moving assets off exchanges does not remove the reliance on centralized infrastructure, because wallets often depend on third-party RPC providers rather than the user’s own node. The issue is not that crypto firms use the cloud but whether they have credible alternatives when it fails, as more assets move onto blockchains. Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” initiative to overhaul its engineering and crisis response following a global service outage that lasted approximately 24 hours. For an industry built around the idea of decentralization, crypto has good reason to pay attention. According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, the technology giant is reconsidering how it prevents and responds to major infrastructure failures after its November 12-13 outage disrupted businesses, government operations and financial firms. Crypto likes to position itself as an alternative to centralized infrastructure. Yet some of its largest businesses depend on the same handful of cloud computing companies, and the consequences of that reliance have already been felt by traders. How A Cooling Failure Brought Coinbase Trading To A Halt In May, Coinbase experienced an infrastructure failure that demonstrated how surprisingly fragile access to cryptocurrency markets can be. The exchange’s official incident report, published on June 1, traced the disruption to a cooling equipment failure inside an Amazon Web Services (AWS) data center. Coinbase had five matching engine nodes located within the same building. Three went offline during the incident, leaving the system without enough functioning nodes to operate normally. The exchange had not implemented an automated mechanism to switch its matching engine to another availability zone. A separate failure involving AWS’s managed event-streaming infrastructure complicated the recovery further. For approximately eight hours, customers experienced severe disruptions affecting trading, deposits and withdrawals. Restoring the remaining systems took roughly another 12 hours. “ “The duration of the outage is unacceptable to us,” Coinbase acknowledged in its subsequent investigation. Coinbase · June 1 incident report This was not the first time the exchange had encountered such problems. An AWS outage in October 2025 resulted in three hours and 17 minutes of degraded performance for Coinbase customers. Despite these incidents, the relationship between cryptocurrency businesses and cloud providers continues to deepen. More recently, Coinbase and AWS partnered to bring x402 payments to CloudFront publishers, bringing blockchain-based payments into existing web infrastructure. The uncomfortable part is that the blockchains themselves did not need to fail for customers to lose access to exchange services. A decentralized settlement network is of limited immediate use to someone whose assets are sitting inside an exchange they cannot access. Your Crypto Wallet May Be Less Decentralized Than You Think Moving assets away from centralized exchanges does reduce some of these risks. However, it does not necessarily eliminate reliance on centralized infrastructure. Consider an Ethereum wallet. When a user opens the application to check their balance or send a transaction, the wallet generally communicates with an Ethereum node through a remote procedure call, commonly known as an RPC. That connection allows the application to retrieve blockchain information and submit signed transactions. How a wallet app connects to Ethereum through an RPC connection. Many users rely on infrastructure operated by third-party providers rather than running their own nodes. If the provider becomes unavailable, the wallet may struggle to display balances or broadcast transactions, even while Ethereum continues producing blocks. In an RPC service outage, the assets can remain intact on the blockchain even when the wallet’s usual connection to the network stops working. Ethereum’s own node documentation acknowledges that widespread reliance on cloud hosting could introduce a common point of failure. Distribution of Ethereum nodes. The distribution of Ethereum nodes also raises questions about infrastructure concentration. Having thousands of independently operated nodes does not necessarily eliminate shared dependencies if many rely on the same hosting providers. Hosting of Ethereum nodes across providers. Shared infrastructure can create security risks as well as availability problems. NewsBTC previously covered the debate over verifier and RPC security following the KelpDAO exploit. That incident was an exploit, not a routine cloud outage. There are alternatives. Users can connect compatible wallets to another RPC provider or operate their own Ethereum nodes. Developers can also design applications to switch between independently operated infrastructure providers when one becomes unavailable. But these options are not always obvious to the average person opening a wallet on their phone. The industry has spent years making crypto easier to use, often by hiding much of its technical complexity. In doing so, it has sometimes reintroduced the dependencies that blockchain technology was intended to reduce. Centralization Is Sometimes A Deliberate Engineering Choice It would be easy to criticize every cryptocurrency company that uses Amazon, Google or Microsoft infrastructure. The reality is more complicated. Coinbase explained that keeping its matching engine nodes physically close together was a deliberate decision intended to meet the speed and capacity requirements of its markets. Separating those systems introduces communication delays. Running redundant infrastructure also costs money, particularly when companies must synchronize large amounts of financial information across multiple locations. Cloud computing providers offer considerable engineering resources and operational capabilities that smaller crypto companies would struggle to reproduce independently. The problem is not simply that crypto businesses use centralized services. It is whether they have credible alternatives when those services fail. Coinbase subsequently outlined plans to improve recovery across availability zones and conduct regular failover exercises in production environments. Those are useful commitments, although publishing a recovery plan and successfully executing one during an unexpected outage are two different things. What Microsoft’s Code Red Means For Crypto There is no established evidence that Microsoft’s latest initiative was prompted by a failure of cryptocurrency networks. The relevance lies elsewhere. As financial institutions bring more assets onto blockchains, the reliability of the infrastructure connecting investors to those networks becomes increasingly important. A tokenized investment fund may exist on a distributed ledger, but investors can still depend on centralized custody providers, banking services, identity verification systems and applications to manage their holdings. A decentralized exchange may execute trades through smart contracts, but its website and the infrastructure connecting users to those contracts can introduce separate vulnerabilities. Crypto companies should be demonstrating how their products behave when their preferred infrastructure provider goes offline. Can users still submit transactions? Can traders cancel orders? Can another operator take over without waiting for an engineering team to intervene? Microsoft’s reported response to its November outage is a reminder that even companies with enormous technical resources can discover weaknesses in systems they previously considered reliable. Crypto does not need to abandon cloud computing. It needs to stop treating decentralization at the blockchain level as proof that everything built around it is equally resilient.

title: BlackRock Launches Hong Kong Tokenized Fund With A HK$10 Entry Point
summary: Key takeaways BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, for investors in Hong Kong. The tokenized D OnChain class lists a minimum investment of HK$10, against HK$10 million for the conventional I class, but access through stablecoins is reportedly limited to professional investors. The fund gives HKDAP, the Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issued by Anchorpoint Financial, a use beyond payments, while the returns still come from the underlying short-term instruments. Tokenization does not remove dealing deadlines or redemption limits, and the disclosures reviewed did not yet give total fund assets or current yields. BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, giving investors in Hong Kong a new way to move money between traditional investments and blockchain-based financial products. The BlackRock tokenized fund, known formally as the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, supports both conventional and tokenized investment units. It also introduces a use case for HKDAP, the Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issued by Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint Financial. The development follows Anchorpoint’s plans to expand HKDAP to Solana, announced in late October. However, there is an interesting detail in BlackRock’s product disclosures. One of the fund’s tokenized classes requires a minimum investment of just HK$10, while access through stablecoins is reportedly limited to professional investors. The technology may be making financial products more accessible, but the institutions behind them still decide who gets through the door. What BlackRock’s New Tokenized Fund Actually Offers BlackRock announced regulatory authorization for the fund on September 10, with its product listings identifying November 16 as the inception date. The commercial launch was reported on Tuesday, November 24. Unlike many of the investment products available across decentralized finance, BlackRock’s fund does not depend on cryptocurrency lending, liquidity pools or token incentives to generate returns. Its investment strategy revolves around short-term financial instruments, including government-backed securities and bank deposits. Investors gain exposure to those assets through fund units. With tokenized units, blockchain technology is used to maintain ownership records. BlackRock’s official product disclosure lists a minimum initial investment of HK$10 for its D OnChain class, alongside a management fee of 0.31% and daily income distributions. BlackRock product disclosure for the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund. Source: BlackRock. For comparison, the fund’s conventional I class requires a minimum initial investment of HK$10 million. The difference is substantial, although a lower investment minimum should not be confused with unrestricted access. Different share classes and distribution channels come with their own conditions. A Stablecoin That Can Finally Do More Than Move Money Perhaps the most interesting part of BlackRock’s launch is what it means for HKDAP. Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture between Standard Chartered, Animoca Brands and HKT, received its stablecoin issuer licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in April. Until now, much of the discussion surrounding regulated Hong Kong dollar stablecoins has focused on payments, transfers and their potential role in financial infrastructure. BlackRock’s fund introduces another practical application. Eligible investors can use digital money denominated in Hong Kong dollars to access investments denominated in the same currency. In its September announcement, BlackRock stated: “ “Investors will be able to use HKDAP” to subscribe to and redeem investments from the fund. BlackRock · September announcement Imagine a company that already holds HKDAP for operational payments. Instead of leaving all its surplus liquidity in stablecoins, it could potentially move some of that balance into a money market fund and earn investment income while the money is not needed. The important distinction is that the stablecoin itself is not generating the fund’s returns. The underlying financial instruments are. Conceptual illustration based on BlackRock’s stated fund structure and digital-cash subscription arrangements. Not a technical settlement architecture or guarantee of immediate redemption. For stablecoin issuers, this kind of integration could ultimately prove more valuable than simply securing another exchange listing. It gives businesses a reason to hold and use digital cash beyond cryptocurrency trading. The Blockchain Is Always Open. The Fund Isn’t. There is still a noticeable difference between what blockchain infrastructure can do and what BlackRock’s product currently offers. The D OnChain class lists a daily dealing schedule with an 11 AM Hong Kong time trading deadline and settlement on the trade date. Anyone familiar with decentralized finance will recognize the contrast. A blockchain does not stop processing transactions because a bank has closed or a fund has passed its dealing deadline. But tokenizing an investment does not automatically change the operating hours, liquidity arrangements or legal obligations of the underlying fund. BlackRock also warns that technology failures, compromised wallets and disruptions involving blockchain service providers could interfere with investors’ ability to access or redeem their holdings. Restrictions on redemptions are possible under stressed market conditions, while investors remain exposed to potential capital losses. These limitations are not necessarily a failure of tokenization. Institutional investors have regulatory, custody and accounting obligations that cannot simply be removed by deploying a smart contract. Still, if investors ultimately have to work around many of the same deadlines and intermediaries they encounter in traditional finance, the immediate advantages of tokenization become narrower. Hong Kong Is Building The Infrastructure Around Tokenized Finance Earlier this month, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority expanded its EnsembleTX settlement initiative to support continuous settlement using tokenized central bank money. The initiative involves several major financial institutions, including BlackRock, and supports applications involving tokenized deposits and investment funds. These developments are gradually connecting different parts of the financial system that previously operated separately. There are now regulated digital currencies, tokenized investment products and settlement infrastructure being developed to move value between them. However, BlackRock’s latest launch also shows why the size of the tokenization market should not be measured solely by the number of financial products being brought onto blockchains. The more interesting figures will be how much money actually enters these funds through digital cash, how frequently investors move between the two products and whether those transactions become cheaper or faster. BlackRock’s product disclosures reviewed for this article did not yet provide usable figures for total fund assets or current yields. Nor does the launch establish unrestricted access through decentralized exchanges or lending protocols. Those are the developments worth watching before declaring that tokenized finance has moved beyond institutional adoption and into the hands of ordinary crypto users. Hong Kong now has another piece of the infrastructure. The next challenge is getting people to use it.

title: Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982
summary: Key takeaways Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday after a Monday recovery above $64,000, while gold is in its own severe correction. Gold fell 24.6% over the 60 days to November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982. Neither asset pays income while interest-bearing investments look more attractive, and selling gold does not automatically send money into Bitcoin. The October PCE report on November 25 is the next test: the previous reading showed headline inflation of 3.6% and core inflation of 3.1%. The Bitcoin price fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, cutting short a recovery that had taken the cryptocurrency above $64,000 a day earlier. But perhaps the more troubling development for investors is happening outside the crypto market. Gold is going through a severe correction of its own, leaving investors in two assets often associated with wealth preservation facing substantial losses. This is not the first time Bitcoin and gold have struggled simultaneously. What makes the current environment particularly difficult is that neither asset generates income at a time when interest-bearing investments offer an increasingly attractive alternative. The question is no longer simply whether Bitcoin is digital gold. It is whether investors have enough reason to own either asset under current monetary conditions. Gold’s Selloff Exposes A Bigger Problem For Bitcoin The selling extended well beyond Bitcoin. Figures from the World Gold Council show that Bitcoin lost 13.7%, gold fell 8.3% and the Nasdaq dropped 10%, while the US Dollar Index gained 0.4%. The numbers point to a broader reduction in risk exposure rather than a selloff specific to crypto. Weekly performance through November 20, 2026. Source: Bloomberg / World Gold Council, Weekly Markets Monitor, November 23, 2026. Gold declined 24.6% over the 60 days ending November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982. The World Gold Council’s latest market assessment, published on Monday, identified several risks facing the precious metal, including pressure on leveraged equity and credit positions, restrictive monetary policy and the possibility of another disappointing US inflation report. The organization also identified the lack of a clear reduction in speculative positioning as a concern. This matters for Bitcoin because the argument for buying BTC during a gold correction often assumes that capital leaving one scarce asset will eventually find its way into the other. There is little reason to assume that happens automatically. An investor selling gold to reduce leverage or meet a margin requirement is unlikely to replace that exposure immediately with Bitcoin. The priority is raising cash, not finding another store of value. There is also a difference between selling an asset because its investment thesis has deteriorated and selling because the cost of maintaining a position has become too expensive. The latter can create opportunities for patient buyers, but it rarely provides a reliable indication of when a market will bottom. Bitcoin’s Recovery Is Still Missing Conviction Monday’s trading session offered Bitcoin investors some encouragement. The cryptocurrency recovered above $64,000 following the previous week’s decline to its lowest levels in roughly two years. The move did not hold. Bitcoin (BTC) price, September 1 to November 21. Source: Coinglass. The broader picture is hardly encouraging. Bitcoin has lost nearly 24% over the past three months, falling from a period high of $86,578 to a low of $58,178. Although BTC has since recovered above $60,000, the bounce has done little to change the broader downward trend. Tuesday’s return below $60,000 raises questions about the strength of the recovery, particularly given the improvement in technology stocks during Monday’s session. If Bitcoin struggles to sustain gains when conditions improve elsewhere, investors should be careful about assuming that another equity market rally will necessarily pull BTC higher. There is also an important distinction between a recovery driven by fresh buyers and one driven by traders closing profitable short positions. Both can produce impressive green candles. Only the former demonstrates that investors are willing to commit new capital at higher prices. Spot trading activity, ETF subscriptions and derivatives positioning will offer a better indication of which type of recovery the market is experiencing. For now, the failure to retain Monday’s gains makes the rebound less convincing than its initial size suggested. Does This Undermine Bitcoin’s Digital Gold Thesis? Bitcoin’s recent performance will inevitably revive criticism of its role as a store of value. However, gold’s own losses make that argument considerably less straightforward. The metal has been used to preserve wealth for centuries, yet it remains vulnerable to changes in interest rates, investor positioning and the strength of the US dollar. Bitcoin shares some of those vulnerabilities while carrying considerably different market risks, including its dependence on speculative demand and the availability of leverage across cryptocurrency exchanges. That does not invalidate Bitcoin’s scarcity argument. Its supply characteristics have not changed because its market price has fallen. What the current correction does challenge is the assumption that scarcity alone guarantees protection during financial stress. An asset can have a credible long-term investment case and still be a poor short-term hedge. Bitcoin investors would benefit from separating those two propositions rather than defending both every time the market declines. The Next Test Comes From The Federal Reserve’s Preferred Inflation Measure The immediate focus now turns to Wednesday’s US inflation release. The Bureau of Economic Analysis is scheduled to publish its October personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report on November 25. The previous release showed annual headline PCE inflation of 3.6%, with core inflation at 3.1%. US personal income and outlays data. Source: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Another stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce expectations of restrictive monetary policy, making conditions more difficult for assets that rely heavily on capital appreciation. A softer reading, particularly if accompanied by falling Treasury yields, could offer some relief to both Bitcoin and gold. For Bitcoin, however, recovering $60,000 should be treated as a starting point rather than confirmation of a broader reversal. Monday’s trading high above $64,000 represents a more demanding test of whether buyers are prepared to return. Until that happens, the market has demonstrated that it can bounce. It has yet to demonstrate that it can sustain a recovery.
